Basic Information for CVE-2026-44494 Vulnerability Information Axios: Full Man-in-the-Middle via Prototype Pollution Gadget in config.proxy Overview A prototype pollution vulnerability exists in the Axios library. Attackers can leverage this vulnerability to escalate to a Man-in-the-Middle (MITM) attack, thereby intercepting, reading, and modifying all HTTP traffic, including authentication credentials. This vulnerability arises because Axios reads config.proxy via standard property access when merging configurations. Since the proxy own property does not exist in the default configuration, it is highly susceptible to malicious proxy address injection via prototype pollution. Affected Versions Affected versions: 1.0.0 to 1.15.x (prior to 1.16.0) Fixed version: 1.16.0 Details Vulnerability Location: Line 670 of lib/adapters/http.js. Trigger Mechanism: The code reads config.proxy using standard property access, which traverses the prototype chain. Injection Principle: The default Axios configuration does not contain a proxy own property. After the configuration object is merged, the proxy property does not exist on the target object itself. Therefore, an attacker only needs to pollute Object.prototype to cause all merged configuration objects to inherit the malicious proxy value. Exploitation Consequence: Through the setProxy() function, all outgoing HTTP requests will be routed to a proxy server controlled by the attacker. Impact Man-in-the-Middle Attack (MITM): Attackers can gain full control over network traffic. Data Leakage: The ability to read all HTTP response content. Credential Theft: Interception and theft of sensitive authentication credentials.
